elements.char: To keep the consistency with the LIF network in which the synapses were current-based (see
elements.label: text

elements.char: Methods), all LFP simulations considered until now were done using current-based synapses
elements.label: text

elements.char: in the 3D network. However, some neuronal features may be better approximated by conduc-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tance-based synaptic models in which the postsynaptic currents (PSCs) depend on the local
elements.label: text

elements.char: membrane potential and do not have a fixed shape as in the case of current-based synapses. To
elements.label: text

elements.char: test this situation, we repeated our simulations by introducing conductance-based synapses in
elements.label: text

elements.char: the 3D network. Synaptic time constants were left unchanged, while the peak conductance val-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ues were scaled to obtain PSC amplitudes equivalent to current-based synapses for the refer-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ence stimulus intensity 1.5 spikes/ms [47].

elements.label: text

elements.char: current-based synapses (compare the three panels in Fig 10A with the three panels in Fig 6B
elements.label: text

elements.char: and note the different y-axis scales), the time course was similar. We found that the explana-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tory power of the proxies was similar or better in all cases compared to the situation with LFPs
elements.label: text

elements.char: computed with current-based synapses (Fig 10A): the R

elements.label: text

elements.char: 0.93 for inputs between 1 and 3 spikes/ms, and 0.88 for 6 spikes/ms. We hypothesize that

elements.label: text
